t: 3773 - Maximum Number of Equal Length Runs
o:
Decompose s into maximal runs of identical letters (e.g., 'hello' → h, e, ll, o), record each run's length, and the answer is the maximum multiplicity of any single length — we select all runs sharing that length.

Example 1: lengths [1,1,2,1] → length 1 appears 3 times → 3. Example 2: lengths [3,1,3] → length 3 appears twice → 2.
k: Runs are determined by a single scan comparing adjacent characters
Answer = max frequency of any run length
At most n runs, so counting is linear

a.i: Walk the string, extending the current run while characters match and closing it otherwise; tally lengths in a hash map and return the largest tally.
s: Initialize len = 1 and an empty counter
For i from 1 to n-1: if s[i] == s[i-1], len++; else increment counter[len], reset len = 1
Increment counter[len] after the loop; return the maximum value in the counter
a.t: O(n) — single scan with O(1) amortized map updates
a.sp: O(n) — at most n distinct run lengths in the map (practically O(√n) since lengths sum to n)

w: Run-length encoding is the whole problem; there is no meaningful alternative approach. Pitfalls: forgetting to flush the final run after the loop, and misreading 'select runs of the same length' as requiring adjacent runs (they don't need to be adjacent). Follow-up: maximum runs selectable if each selected run must have a distinct letter, or selecting runs across multiple strings.
